conventions.render: drawn at 1080 px (2x), reduced once to 540 px (Lanczos, premultiplied)
conventions.frame_time: frame f (from panel start) shows the state at t=f+1 frames; stroke visible from on_frame, complete at done_frame
conventions.outline: stroke 0 contour t 0-4.5 f, 2-frame pen lift, stroke 1 tail stub t 6.5-8.0 f: outline complete at frame 7, letters start at t=8
conventions.pen_rate: 9.0 letters/s (alphanumerics), punctuation and lifts inside that budget; capped so the required post-balloon hold fits the plan.json panel slot
conventions.lifts: 2-frame pen lift between words and between lines; 0.4 frame between strokes inside a word (see amendments.md: a literal 2-frame lift between every stroke cannot meet 9 glyphs/s)
conventions.boil: #38 DP over 3 hand variants (v0 canonical + 2 redraws), min hold 2 frames, flicker cost, frozen through the B4 pen hold; only while writing; frame >= end_frame is exactly the PNG
conventions.composite: out = (art*(255-a) + c*a + 127)//255 on L; colour channels R=G=B; balloon ink and paper values taken from plate.json (see plate_used_for_checks)
conventions.placement_rule: never cover eye, flap, lamp globe; tails short stubs aimed at the snout; no tail crosses the ear box

beats.speaker: creature
beats.line: IF I OPEN IT, / I'LL KNOW.
beats.intention: name the stakes: opening the envelope ends uncertainty
beats.transition: listener learns the envelope matters and that knowing is feared, not wanted

beats.speaker: creature
beats.line: IF I DON'T, / I CAN STILL / HOPE.
beats.intention: argue for the other branch: not opening keeps hope alive
beats.transition: the sideways eye now reads as longing over the letter; the reader expects a choice

beats.speaker: creature
beats.transition: nothing is said and nothing moves: the reader supplies the decision; the silence is the choice being made

beats.speaker: creature
beats.transition: the unchanged half-lidded eye now reads as resignation; the letter will stay shut

beats.speaker: creature
beats.line: ME? I'VE BEEN / ON THIS BENCH / SINCE NINE.
beats.intention: deflect an accusation with a time alibi
beats.transition: reader infers an off-panel accuser and a crime; the same pose becomes a witness stand

beats.speaker: creature
beats.intention: cite the picture itself as witness (the lamp, uncovered top-left)
beats.transition: reader looks at the lamp; the drawing is now evidence, and the joke is that a lamp cannot testify

beats.speaker: creature
beats.intention: offer the sealed flap as proof of innocence
beats.transition: reader checks the flap (uncovered) and half-accepts the alibi

beats.speaker: creature
beats.line: WHY WOULD I / OPEN SOMEONE / ELSE'S?
beats.transition: volunteers that the envelope is not its own: the alibi collapses; the identical sideways eye now reads as guilt (not 'continue': the meaning of the eye flips)

arc-1 (chosen): IF I OPEN IT, / I'LL KNOW.
IF I DON'T, / I CAN STILL / HOPE.
arc-2 (branch-a, kept, lettered): SHE ONLY WRITES / TO SAY / GOODBYE.
A.judgement: arc-1 keeps the reference shape (dilemma, dilemma, silence, deflating short line) and makes the silence the decision itself. arc-2 is stronger as story (a reason to fear the letter) but its last line changes the subject rather than resolving the dilemma, and it gives the envelope a sender, which would pre-empt strip B's "someone else's". Kept as branch-a.

arc-1 (chosen; B1-B3 locked): ME? I'VE BEEN / ON THIS BENCH / SINCE NINE.
WHY WOULD I / OPEN SOMEONE / ELSE'S?
arc-2 (branch-b, kept, B4 lettered): ME? I'VE BEEN / ON THIS BENCH / SINCE NINE.
WHO SAID / ANYTHING ABOUT / A LETTER?
B.judgement: arc-1's B4 turns the alibi into a confession through ownership: the reader re-reads the eye as guilt. branch-b B4 (over-denial) is funny but the accuser never mentioned a letter only if we assume so; it is less sure to flip the eye. arc-3 spends the lamp too late and loses the hinge.
